title: Expiration Notice Timing and the Renewal Starting Rate — Residential Natural Gas Supply
content:
When a Residential Natural Gas Supply agreement is renewed within its term, the timing and the rates of its two expiration notices decide the renewal starting rate, the per-therm rate from which the renewal acceptance rate is figured.

## When a notice is on time

An expiration notice is on time when the initial renewal notice is dated between 60 and 45 calendar days, both included, before the contract end date it names, and when the final options notice is dated at least 30 calendar days before that date and later than the initial renewal notice. These figures are the same on every Residential Natural Gas Supply plan.

## The starting rate

When both expiration notices were on time and the final options notice states a higher renewal rate than the initial renewal notice, the renewal starting rate is the lower of the two stated rates; when the initial renewal notice was on time and the final options notice was not, the renewal starting rate is the initial renewal notice's rate; in every other case the renewal starting rate is the final options notice's rate.

| Initial renewal notice on time | Final options notice on time | Final rate higher than initial rate | Renewal starting rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | the lower of the two (the initial renewal notice's rate) |
| Yes | Yes | No | the final options notice's rate |
| Yes | No | any | the initial renewal notice's rate |
| No | Yes | any | the final options notice's rate |
| No | No | any | the final options notice's rate |

The records read are the most recent initial renewal notice and the most recent final options notice on the agreement, each with its notice date, the contract end date it names and its renewal rate.

## Worked cases (hypothetical; contract end date 30 September)

- Initial notice dated 5 August at 0.7900, final options notice dated 25 August at 0.8150: both on time and the final rate is higher, so the starting rate is 0.7900.
- Initial notice dated 5 August at 0.8200, final dated 25 August at 0.8050: both on time, final not higher, so 0.8050.
- Initial notice dated 5 August at 0.7900, final dated 3 September (27 days before) at 0.8150: the final is not on time, so 0.7900.
- Initial notice dated 20 August (41 days before) at 0.7900, final dated 25 August at 0.8150: the initial is not on time, so 0.8150.
